# 4 Ezra Chapter 7 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 7:28 — "my son the Messiah" (filius meus Iesus)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my son the Messiah" | Follows Syriac/Ethiopic; avoids Latin Iesus interpolation |
| LOGOS | "my son the Messiah" | Same — scholarly consensus that "Jesus" is a scribal addition |
| PNEUMA | "my son the Messiah" | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Unanimous: "my son the Messiah." The Latin filius meus Iesus uses Iesus as the Latin form of the Hebrew Messiah, not the NT figure; "Messiah" is the more transparent rendering here.

---

## 7:36 — Gehenna / pit of torment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pit-of-torment...furnace-of-Gehenna" | Preserves Latin lacus tormenti, caminus Gehennae |
| LOGOS | "pit of torment...furnace of Gehenna" | Same without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "pit of torment...furnace of Gehenna" | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Unanimous. "Gehenna" preserved as proper name throughout.

---

## 7:40–43 — the cosmic nihil-list (no sun/moon/stars, etc.)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full hyphenated list | Literal |
| LOGOS | Full list without hyphens | Clean formal list |
| PNEUMA | Full list without hyphens, same order | Same |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS rendering. The list is one of the most striking passages in the book; preserving each element without abbreviation is essential.

---

## 7:85–91 — the seven orders of the righteous

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "first-order, second-order" etc. with hyphens | Literal Latin ordinis |
| LOGOS | "first order, second order" etc. | Standard |
| PNEUMA | "First stage, second stage" etc. | "Stage" is more natural for a progressive spiritual journey |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "First order, second order" (LOGOS). "Order" preserves the structural/hierarchical sense of the Latin ordo.

---

## 7:112 — Adam lament: "the evil was not yours alone"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the evil was-not-yours-alone: it-is-also-ours" | Literal, with hyphens |
| LOGOS | "the fall was not yours alone — it is also ours" | Substitutes "fall" for "evil" to capture peccatum |
| PNEUMA | "the consequences were not yours alone; they fall on all of us" | Paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The fall was not yours alone — it is also ours who are your descendants" (LOGOS). "Fall" is the most appropriate theological term for peccatum in this context.

---

## 7:126 — intercession cut off / joy of the saved over the lost

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-shall-not-fast for-those-who-perished, but-they-shall-joy over-them" | Literal; "fast" translates ieiunabunt |
| LOGOS | "they shall not grieve for those who perish, but shall rejoice" | Interprets ieiunabunt as mourning fasting |
| PNEUMA | "they will not mourn for those who perish — they will rejoice" | Same interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "They shall not grieve for those who perish, but shall rejoice" (LOGOS). The Latin ieiunabunt likely means fasting as mourning practice here; "grieve" captures the function better than the literal "fast."

---

## Total disagreements: 6
